decisionsTitle: «Până când»: every row says the instant it waits on, in the list and the export (amending §635)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-03:** «Vreau să văd exact pe fiecare candidat până când poate semna declarația».

**What the backoffice said until now (§635).** For one chosen event, the grouped block «Când se pierde un loc» said how many wait on each deadline; the list's step cell «Unde a ajuns» added the row's deadline after the step («3/6 · Loc rezervat · ține locul până …»), and the registration's timeline said «Ține locul până». The moment per person was there, but inside a sentence of another column: not a column of its own, not sortable, not in the export. An organizer on the phone with a participant, or looking for who signs next, had to read every step cell.

**Decision: one helper, one column, «Până când» / “Until when”.** This amends §635: its block stays, its rules stay; the step cell's deadline moves to the column.
- `registrations/domain/row-deadline.ts#rowDeadlineOf` is pure: a row's status, `hold_expires_at`, `email_link_expires_at`, whether its offer's first email is still queued, and the clock in; the one moment the row waits on out, with its kind — `hold` / `kept` (a place held for the declaration, before and past its deadline: past it the place is kept while nobody asks for it, §160, so the person can still sign), `offer` / `offerLapsed` (a waiting-list offer, §520), `reserved` (a family's reservation while it holds, §543), `link` / `linkLapsed` (the first email's link, §377, from when the email left, §513). Every other state — waiting, confirmed, ended — waits on none.
- **An offer whose `WAITLIST_SPOT_OFFER` is still queued has not lapsed** (§520), whatever its stored deadline says: it still occupies its place, the sweep leaves it, and the send re-bases the deadline. The night's hourly tick, or a short window under the governor's floor (§447), makes exactly this case. The list's query and the registration's page read it as one correlated `EXISTS` on the row (`offerEmailQueued`, the allocator's own `repository.ts#offerAwaitingItsFirstEmail`) — no query per row — and such an offer stays `offer`: «Poate accepta până …», never «termenul ofertei a trecut».
- **The column**, «Până când» / “Until when” (`?sort=untilWhen`), right after «Unde a ajuns», over one event or every event: each row's own moment is true of that row, unlike §635's block, which is why that one stays on a single event. One definition, so the phone layout carries it too (§53). The cell is one sentence with the exact instant (`formatDay`, short, with the time): «Poate semna până {instant}», «Poate accepta până {instant}», «Locul e rezervat până {instant}», «Linkul e valabil până {instant}»; past it, in grey, the instant first: «{instant} — termenul a trecut, locul e păstrat», «{instant} — termenul ofertei a trecut», «{instant} — linkul a expirat». «—» on a row that waits on nothing, as the race number's column says it. A «?» beside the heading says how to read it, and that the registration's timeline says the same instant.
- **«până {instant}», not the brief's «până la {instant}».** The instant carries its weekday and, inside a sentence, its own «la» before the hour (§452: «până sâm., 3 oct. 2026, la 14:00»); «până la sâm., …, la 14:00» says «la» twice, and §452 refuses «până la» before a deadline with its hour (`date-prepositions.test.ts`, which now reads `{instant}` too). The offer's lapse reads «termenul ofertei a trecut» rather than «oferta a expirat»: the words claim only what the row says.
- **Sortable** (`admin-repository.ts#rowDeadlineOrder`): the same cases in SQL, with the page's clock deciding a reservation against its link, so the order is the order of the instants on screen; the soonest first, and the rows with none last in both directions, like the race number (§173). Opens ascending: the person about to lose a place is the one asked about.
- **The step's cell says the step alone.** «3/6 · Loc rezervat» and its hover title; the deadline it carried since §635 is the column's now — the same instant twice on one phone card is noise. The registration's full journey keeps its deadlines.
- **The export carries the moment and what it is for.** The spreadsheet puts «Until when» (the club's clock, §439) and «Waiting on» (the kind in words: “can sign the declaration until”, “deadline passed, the place is kept”, “can accept the offer until”, “the offer's deadline has passed”, “the place is reserved until”, “the link is valid until”, “the link has expired”) right after «Status», as the list puts the column beside the state — it is matched by header, as the socials column beside Instagram is (§500). The CSV ends with the same two, «Until when» in ISO 8601 and «Waiting on» as the kind's stable token (`hold`, `kept`, `offer`, `offerLapsed`, `reserved`, `link`, `linkLapsed`), last because a script reads the CSV by position (§425). Both empty on a row that waits on none.
- **The registration's timeline** reads the same helper: «Ține locul până» on a place the row still holds (a kept hold adds the journey's words), «Rezervarea expiră» on a lapsed offer — which `countOccupied` no longer counts — as on an ended row.

Read from the row: no join, no query per row. Every role that reads the list reads the column, the Organizer too (§289); it shows a moment and a state, never an address (§15.11). A test registration shows its deadline like any row, under its chip (§30); the export omits it as before.

*Rejected:*
- **Keeping the deadline in the step's cell as well.** Two copies of one instant per row.
- **A countdown («în 2 zile»).** §635 refused it; the owner asked for the exact moment.
- **A «Până când» column on the race-day desk.** On race day every hold, offer and link is decided: the sweep has run, the close has passed (§420), and the desk confirms, gives a free place or checks in on the spot (§15.11) — none of it waits on an instant. The desk also shows every staff role, the Tehnic one included, only a name, a state and a number; the list, which the Organizer reads, is where the question «până când» is asked.
- **Moving a declaration hold's instant while its first email is still queued** (§513: its send moves the deadline forward). The column says the hold's stored instant; past it, «termenul a trecut, locul e păstrat» is true either way — a hold is kept past its deadline until somebody needs the place (§160), and one whose email is queued is not even swept. The offer is different: past its deadline it lapses, so for it the queued email is read (above).
changelogLine: - **Every registration says until when** — the registrations list has a «Până când» column: to the minute, until when each person can sign the declaration, accept an offer or confirm the address, and what a passed deadline means; sortable, on the phone too, and in the export beside the status as «Until when» and «Waiting on». §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the registrations list, over one event or every event, when it renders, then a column «Până când» / “Until when”, right after «Unde a ajuns» and in the phone layout too, says on each row the instant it waits on, read from the row with no query per row: a held place's «Poate semna până {instant}» or, past it, «{instant} — termenul a trecut, locul e păstrat»; an open offer's «Poate accepta până {instant}» or «{instant} — termenul ofertei a trecut», an offer whose first email is still queued reading as open (§520); a family's reservation «Locul e rezervat până {instant}» while it holds; else the first email's link «Linkul e valabil până {instant}» or «{instant} — linkul a expirat»; «—» on every other row. `?sort=untilWhen` orders by the same instant, the soonest first and the rows with none last either way; the step's cell says the step alone, in place of criterion 11's deadline in the list's cell; the registration's timeline reads «Rezervarea expiră» on a lapsed offer (2026-10-03, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the registrations export, when it is produced, then it carries the list's «Până când» as two columns, «Until when» and «Waiting on»: in the spreadsheet right after «Status», the instant on the club's clock and what it is for in words; in the CSV last, the instant in ISO 8601 and the kind's token (`hold`, `kept`, `offer`, `offerLapsed`, `reserved`, `link`, `linkLapsed`); both empty on a row that waits on none (2026-10-03, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: each registration says until when, in the list's «Până când» column and the export
